newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian shares gain as vouchers lose appeal.
newsitem.headline: Latvian shares gain as vouchers lose appeal.

text.p: Latvian stock prices advanced on Wednesday and buyers were seen slowly returning to the bourse as voucher prices reach unattractive levels, dealers said.
Total turnover fell to 63,000 lats from 125,000 lats.
The Rietumu index added 2.98 percent to 181.26 and the Saule10 closed at 141.16, up 3.21 percent.
"Dealers were mostly smiling today as funds were seen coming back to the market from the rival voucher market," Aldis Sipols, securities department head of the Savings Bank (Krajbanka), told Reuters.
The voucher market is comprised of privatisation vouchers issued by the state to individuals.
"The current price of 2.70 lats a voucher is too expensive for those wanting to exchange them for shares and nothing much in terms of big privatisation is expected during the summer," he said.
Riga Shipyard was the most traded stock on volume of 17,500 lats and it rose to 1.35 lats from 1.32 lats.
All official list stocks gained ground and the Riga Transport Fleet saw 9,100 lats of shares traded and it added two santimes to 1.28 lats.
Unibanka jumped to 3.16 lats from 3.01 lats on trade of 3,200 lats while Staburadze had volume of 3,700 lats.
It advanced three santimes to 2.53 lats.
A smaller stock, Strenchi Forestry, dominated the secondary list on good first quarter results.
It registered trade of 11,500 lats and jumped to 1.43 lats or 14 percent, adding 18 santimes.
Strenchi earlier reported a first quarter profit of 130,878 lats.
